evidence: naemon-contact-file (manifests/user_sysmon.pp:14-18): the file resource declares /etc/naemon/conf.d/contacts/${myusername}.cfg mode 0664 owner/group naemon with the sysmon_contact.erb content; the probe stats the p8testuser file and expects 'naemon naemon 664', matching.

naemon-contact-file (templates/users/sysmon_contact.erb:1-7): the template renders define contact / use generic-contact / contact_name @myusername / alias @myname / email @myemail / contactgroups @mygrouplist; with the params fixture (Puppet 8 Test User, root@localhost, [admins]) and whitespace normalised by sed, the expected text including the Array#to_s rendering ["admins"] is what the template produces.

thruk-htpasswd-entry (manifests/user_sysmon.pp:11-12): htpasswd { $myusername: cryptpasswd => $myhash, target => '/etc/thruk/htpasswd' } writes <user>:<hash>; the probe greps the p8testuser line and keeps the first three $-fields, expecting p8testuser:$6$p8testsalt, which is the prefix of the fixture's myhash.

the-thruk-entry-accepts-the-password (mutating, line 12, read whole file): mutates declares the apache2-utils install and the /run/p8test-sysmon/verify.txt output; the action is two read-only htpasswd -v verifications of the file the htpasswd resource writes; the effect reads the recorded verdicts. The wrong-password verification (expected 'password verification failed', rc=3) is an in-probe mismatch: changing the password changes the verdict, so the check cannot pass on a hash that accepts anything. Invariant/why_invariant: none in the set; no probe reaches another host.
